---
title: Start a deck
---

Make a short presentation, choose a ready-made theme, and open it with your
speaker notes. You write Markdown; the bundled theme supplies the appearance.
The finished deck runs in a browser.

## 1. Run the example

Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and
[Just](https://just.systems/man/en/), then clone this repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/htmpres.git
cd htmpres
just example
```

This creates `decks/example/index.html` for the audience and
`decks/example/presenter.html` with speaking cues. Open either file in your
browser. Use Right or Space to advance; some slides have several reveal steps.

You can try the same patterns online first: [open the interactive example](example.qmd?slide=5).
Its controls work directly on the page, and its Markdown shows how each slide
was written. [Compare themes](compare.qmd) when you want to choose an appearance.

## 2. Create your talk

From the repository folder, run:

```sh
quarto run scripts/htmpres.ts deck new decks/my-talk --title "My first talk" --theme nocturne
```

The command creates `decks/my-talk/index.qmd`, a starter stylesheet and an
`assets/` folder. Leave the stylesheet as supplied. Open `index.qmd` in your
text editor and replace its contents with this complete three-slide talk:

````markdown
---
pagetitle: "My first talk"
deck:
  theme: nocturne
  color-mode: auto
---

## Give the audience a *clear claim*

[One useful idea is enough to begin.]{.key}

[Put qualifications in supporting text.]{.aside}

::: notes
Explain why this idea matters to this audience.
:::

## Show the evidence in order

::: {.incremental data-fragment-effect="dim"}
- State the question.
- Show the evidence.
- Explain what it means.
:::

::: notes
Advance once for each point. Pause before the implication.
:::

## Leave them with the result

[The evidence supports the claim.]{.key}

Questions?
````

Each `##` starts a slide. Markdown emphasis works in titles. `.key` marks the
main point; `.aside` marks supporting context. The incremental list hides
future points and dims earlier ones. The theme decides how these roles look.

A `::: notes` block belongs to the preceding slide. It appears only in the
presenter output. Use top-level `---` or `##` for the next slide. A separator
followed by a heading, with only blank lines between, makes one slide. For
untitled-slide settings use `## {#backup data-kind="appendix"}`. The initial
YAML delimiters and rules inside code, comments or fenced divs do not split
slides. See [the full boundary contract](semantic-authoring.md#slide-boundaries-and-lint).

## 3. Preview while you write

```sh
quarto run scripts/htmpres.ts serve decks/my-talk/index.qmd --watch --port 8000
```

Open [the audience view](http://127.0.0.1:8000/) and
[the presenter view](http://127.0.0.1:8000/presenter.html) on your own computer
while the command is running. The presenter page includes the same slides and
their cues. The two windows navigate independently.

Change a heading or a cue and save `index.qmd`. Both pages rebuild and reload
automatically, keeping their current slide. Reveal steps restart on that
slide. If a save contains an error, the terminal explains it and the last good
deck stays visible. Correct the source and save again. Stop the preview with
Ctrl+C.

## 4. Choose a bundled theme and mode

Change the existing `deck` entries at the top of `index.qmd`, for example:

```yaml
deck:
  theme: simplex-reading
  color-mode: auto
```

Save and watch the preview change. Keep the other metadata and slides; there
should be only one `deck` block. You can choose Nocturne, Simplex Reading or
another name in the [theme catalog](themes.md#available-names).

| Setting | Result |
|---|---|
| `color-mode: light` | Use light as the deck's default. |
| `color-mode: dark` | Use dark as the deck's default. |
| `color-mode: auto` | Follow the system preference unless the reader has chosen a mode. |

Viewers can use the deck's mode button; their choice is remembered for that
deck. The 35 paired themes provide both modes. The three legacy seeds are light
only. Selecting a bundled theme by name is all you need for normal use.

## 5. Add a pattern when you need it

The [interactive example](example.qmd) shows the source together with the
rendered slide. Copy the slide's Markdown, paste it after your existing slides,
and replace its content:

- [Code and explaining text](example.qmd?slide=5): step a line highlight and its explanation together.
- [A stepped equation](example.qmd?slide=6): typeset math and emphasize named terms in order.
- [Speaker notes](example.qmd?slide=8): switch between audience and presenter views of one source.
- [Appendix links](example.qmd?slide=10): keep supporting detail after the main ending and return to the result.

For a simple two-column slide, append:

```markdown
## Compare two options

:::: {.two-col}
::: {}
### First option

The first argument.
:::
::: {}
### Second option

The second argument.
:::
::::
```

For a local image, put the file in your talk's `assets/` folder and write
`![A description of the image](assets/result.svg){.zoomable}`. The description
helps readers using assistive tools; clicking a zoomable image opens it larger.

## 6. Check and share

```sh
just render decks/my-talk/index.qmd
just verify decks/my-talk/index.qmd
```

Render writes `index.html` and `presenter.html` beside your source. Verify
checks that the generated views match that source. To check slide breaks with
machine-readable output, use `just lint decks/my-talk/index.qmd`.

For an offline audience copy, share `index.html` together with its generated
`assets/` folder, preserving the relative paths. Keep `presenter.html` and your
QMD source for yourself when the speaking cues should stay private. The assets
include the fonts and math files needed by the deck.

You now have an editable talk, a theme, an audience page and a presenter page.
Use the [semantic authoring guide](semantic-authoring.md) for further syntax,
or the [class reference](quarto-class-map.md) to look up a layout.

[Customization reference](build-a-deck-from-markdown.md) covers optional theme
and layout overrides. [Website maintenance](contributing.md) covers building
this documentation site.
